recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for core reconciliation. Future semantic or editorial changes to these extension definitions should be made in HL7/fhir-extensions; separate later work such as FHIR-49864 should proceed through its own Jira/application path.
issue_request: FHIR-20469 was a Published/Persuasive Pharmacy change request for MedicationDispense, raised in STU3 and applied for R5, asking to bring the STU3 refills remaining extension back into core extensions and add a new quantity remaining extension.
initial_application: The Jira application comment cites merge commit 16680e7ffc2f0f3b8cf031ce23e828ec14c2457e. The implementation history around 92cc8632039c231c346b3ab90697c9c0537a1a5f shows GF/FHIR-20469 was applied with other Pharmacy changes, and later generated core definitions existed for medicationdispense-refillsRemaining and medicationdispense-quantityRemaining until the R5 extension-source removal.
additional_context: MedicationDispense and pharmacy-core remain active in source/fhir.ini, and core retains OID registrations for both extension URLs, but current core source contains no active definitions for the two MedicationDispense remaining/refills extensions. Commit dd468d4f1799dd79819315b211588ef1cf4586e0 intentionally removed generated extension definitions from R5 core source. The current read-only HL7/fhir-extensions checkout contains both canonical extension definitions with MedicationDispense context and the expected integer and SimpleQuantity value types. Later FHIR-49864 and related community discussion concern separate repeat/refill modeling and are not Applied/Published source-edit decisions for this seed.
reconciliation: No core source was changed. The core combined branch received an empty external-repo audit commit because the requested extension artifacts now belong in the FHIR Extension Pack and are already present there.
